summary: Reference for the Water plugin's Water Body actor types (Ocean, Lake, River, Custom, Island, Exclusion Volume): how each is defined by splines, how they carve Landscape via a brush, and all per-body properties for spline points, terrain carving curves/falloff/effects, waves, materials and underwater post process.
gotchas: Landscape carving only works when the Landscape has Enable Edit Layers checked
Custom water bodies do not use the Water Mesh Actor and do not carve terrain
Keep the Elevation Curve Y value at 1 for River spline Depth values to be accurate
Exclusion Volumes need Exclude All Overlapping Water Bodies or the Water Bodies to Exclude array set

summary: Shows how to make physics objects float on Water Bodies using the Buoyancy component's sphere pontoons, with a step-by-step Blueprint setup, the BP_BuoyancyExample sample, a full property table (buoyancy, drag, river forces) and debug drawing.
gotchas: Mass (kg) override must be enabled on the Static Mesh for buoyancy to work
The Static Mesh must be the root component
Pontoon relative locations have no viewport visualization; use sockets or Scene components to place them

summary: Lists the Water system's stat commands and r.Water console variables for debugging (tile bounds, wireframe, underwater post process, frozen waves, buoyancy) and for scaling quality/cost (LOD/tessellation bias, shallow water sim, spline resampling distance).
gotchas: Water is excluded from ray tracing by default (r.RayTracing.Geometry.Water 0)
After changing r.Water.WaterSplineResampleMaxDistance you must edit the water spline to see the result
Too low a resample distance can cause missing water tiles; 50 is recommended
Disable underwater post process if the camera never goes below the surface

summary: Explains how the Water Zone generates a shared tiled, LOD-morphing surface mesh for all Water Bodies (LODScale, Tessellation Factor, Tile Size, Extent in Tiles, Far Distance mesh), the Water_Material instances and river transition materials, underwater post processing, and requirements for custom water materials.
gotchas: A Water Zone must be in the level for Water Body surfaces to render
High tessellation and large extents significantly impact performance
Underwater post process requires Generate Collision enabled
Custom water materials need the Used with Water usage flag

summary: How-to for building a reusable User Widget button (CustomButton) with an instance-editable style variable and an Event Dispatcher so each placed instance can respond differently, then adding it to a HUD widget created from the Level Blueprint.
gotchas: Use the variable Set Style node, not the Button function node
Without an Event Dispatcher every button instance runs the same OnClicked logic

summary: Explains UMG Slots, the per-parent layout properties (e.g. Canvas Panel Slot anchors vs Grid Slot row/column) shown under the Slot category, and how to change them at runtime by casting a widget's Slot to the right slot type.
gotchas: In Blueprints only setter nodes are exposed for slot layout properties; store values in your own variable if you need to read them

summary: Covers the Widget Interaction component, which raycasts from a pawn/weapon/mouse to in-world Widget Components and simulates key or pointer presses on them; includes property and Blueprint node references.
gotchas: Interaction Source Custom requires calling SetCustomHitResult()
Use Send Key Char rather than Press Key for a-z/A-Z text input
Works at the Slate level, so it cannot report which widget is under the hit

summary: Basic intro to creating a Widget Blueprint from the Content Browser and a tour of the Widget Blueprint Editor panels (Designer/Graph modes, Palette, Hierarchy, Visual Designer, Details, Animations).
Short property reference for the Widget Component, which renders a Widget Blueprint in the 3D world (World space, occludable) or on screen (Screen space) from an actor.
gotchas: Draw at Desired Size is expensive if done every frame
Screen space widgets are never occluded; World space widgets can be

summary: Step-by-step CommonUI setup: switching the game viewport client to CommonGameViewportClient, building CommonInputActionDataBase data tables, a CommonUIInputData asset for default Click/Back, per-platform CommonInputBaseControllerData icon assets, and Common Style assets/template styles.
gotchas: A custom viewport client must extend CommonGameViewportClient
CommonUI Input Action Data Tables are unrelated to Enhanced Input / project input actions
Default Gamepad Name must exactly match a Controller Data asset's Gamepad Name or icons will not appear
CommonUI widgets lack base UMG styling options and use Common Style assets instead

summary: Deep technical walkthrough of CommonUI's input pipeline: how the synthetic analog cursor turns gamepad Accept into mouse clicks, how navigation focus moves, how the Action Router routes input through the Activatable Widget node tree, and which classes to subclass to customise it.
gotchas: Game viewport class must be the CommonUI viewport client for routing to work
Input processors run on all input including the Unreal Editor
Deactivated widgets are never considered for input routing
Overriding the action router means the base one's ShouldCreateSubsystem won't create an instance

summary: FAQ-style guidance on whether to adopt CommonUI (multi-layer menus, cross-platform), migrating, when to use CommonActivatableWidget vs CommonUserWidget, and why simultaneous mouse and keyboard-as-gamepad navigation is unsupported.
gotchas: CommonUI does not work with widgets placed in the world via WidgetComponents
Simultaneous mouse and keyboard navigation is not supported; toggling between them is fine
May not be worth it for single-layer, PC-only UIs

summary: Tips for debugging CommonUI input without breakpoints disturbing focus (hit-count and Widget Reflector [CBP] conditional breakpoints), plus FAQ on UI not working while paused, analog inputs in key handlers, and game input in Menu mode.
gotchas: CommonUI relies on LocalPlayerSubsystems that don't tick when the game is paused; set actors/widgets tickable when paused
Game input is allowed in Menu mode when the viewport has mouse capture; disable viewport mouse capture in the input config to stop it

summary: Explains how CommonBoundActionBar gathers actions marked Display In Action Bar from active widgets into an on-screen button-hint bar, and how to set it up with a UCommonBoundActionButton subclass.
gotchas: The Common Text Widget must be named Text_ActionName or the Blueprint fails to compile
The bar does not update while the game is paused because it relies on local player tick
Widgets must be activated (Activatable Widgets start deactivated)

Practical UMG authoring tips: pick one target resolution and DPI scale 1.0, prepare UI textures without built-in padding and use Draw As Border for tiling, Auto vs Fill slot sizing, Scale Box instead of render transforms for permanent scaling, editor shortcuts, reusable User Widgets and basic optimizations.
gotchas: Render Transforms are not part of layout, so they won't scale correctly across resolutions; use a Scale Box for permanent scaling
Authoring widgets at different screen sizes or scales leads to inconsistent scaling

summary: Empty hub page (title and description only) for the UMG (Unreal Motion Graphics) editor reference; no content or links in the extract.
Empty hub page (title and description only) for importing and editing fonts in the Unreal Editor; no content or links in the extract.
Empty hub page (title and description only) for the reference of UMG widget types; no content or links in the extract.

Shows how to display a Widget Blueprint at runtime with Create Widget and Add to Viewport, remove it with Remove from Parent, control input with the Set Input Mode nodes and Set Show Mouse Cursor, and nest widgets with Add Child/RemoveChild.
keys: Set Input Mode Game and UI
gotchas: Set Input Mode UIOnly disables all game controls; use sparingly
Store the Create Widget return value in a variable to reuse or remove it later instead of re-creating

summary: Explains the UI Invalidation system that caches widget hierarchy/layout/paint data to cut CPU cost: Invalidation Box, Global Invalidation, Retainer Panels, the cost of each invalidation type, and marking frequently-changing widgets Volatile.
gotchas: Global Invalidation deactivates any Invalidation Boxes inside the window
Retainer Panels have high repaint overhead and extra memory (own render target); try Invalidation Boxes first
Adding/removing children every frame (Child Invalidation) is a major bottleneck

summary: UMG/Slate performance guidelines: use invalidation and Volatile, avoid Tick/OnPaint and property bindings in favour of events, trim and async-load widgets, limit Canvas Panels/Overlays, prefer Spacers over Size Boxes, avoid Scale Box+Size Box combos, limit Rich Text, and the relative CPU cost of widget animation methods.
gotchas: Never use raw attribute binding; it polls every frame
Canvas Panels increment Layer IDs and add draw calls; don't nest them in small custom widgets
Combining Scale Boxes and Size Boxes can loop, flipping size every frame
Sequencer UMG animations have a startup cost and render-transform animations invalidate layout each frame

summary: C++ reference for Slate's sleep mode and Active Timers: registering/unregistering FWidgetActiveTimerDelegate timers on SWidgets so editor UI only ticks when needed, FCurveSequence integration, and the cvars to test sleeping.
gotchas: Intended for editor UI, not game UI with a real-time viewport
Any single active timer wakes all of Slate
Duplicate registrations are possible; track registration with a flag or weak handle
An active timer's period cannot be changed after registration; unregister and re-register

summary: Hub/overview for the CommonUI plugin: lists its features (Common UI widget library, style data assets, Input Routing, platform-specific button icons, gamepad cardinal navigation) and points to its subpages.

High-level overview of the C++ Slate UI framework with code samples for its declarative syntax macros, composition with SNew and slots, style sets, layout primitives, docking tabs and the Widget Reflector.

C++ Slate code examples: common widget arguments, Visibility and alignment values, box panels and slot sizing, SUniformGridPanel, SWrapBox, radio buttons via check boxes, menus/context menus/toolbars with multibox builders, and SListView/STreeView/STileView item views.
gotchas: UI_COMMAND commands cannot be used with dynamically generated buttons/controls
Tile views do not support columns or column headers

summary: Design principles of Slate: polling via delegates and TAttribute over cached state, when to invalidate, child slots and widget roles (leaf, panel, compound), the two-pass layout (ComputeDesiredSize then ArrangeChildren), OnPaint draw-element generation, and composition.
gotchas: Large numbers of off-screen live widgets can severely hurt Slate performance; virtualize scrolling content

summary: Shows the Build.cs module dependencies needed to use Slate from C++: InputCore as public, Slate and SlateCore as private (often present but commented out).

C++ guide to showing raw Slate widgets in-game: Build.cs Slate dependencies, then adding/removing widgets on GEngine->GameViewport with AddViewportWidgetContent (with Z-order), RemoveViewportWidgetContent and RemoveAllViewportWidgets.
gotchas: GEngine and GameViewport can be NULL; always check before use
Higher Z-order values draw on top; default Z-order is 0

summary: Explains Slate Clipping 2.0 (scissor rects and stencil quads, render-space clipping), the EWidgetClipping modes, migrating from pre-4.17 APIs, custom clipping in OnPaint with PushClip/PopClip, culling with IsChildWidgetCulled, and clipping debug cvars.
gotchas: SScissorRectBox and passing clip rects to FSlateDrawElement::Make are deprecated
Slate can no longer batch across clipping zones
A child is culled when its parent is culled, even if transformed outside the parent's bounds

summary: Guide to the Widget Reflector debugging tool for Slate/UMG: opening it, picking painted or hit-testable widgets, focus display, Slate debug flags (show clipping, debug culling, invalidation/paint debugging), texture/font atlases, snapshots and widget event logs.
gotchas: Snapshots can only be taken in PIE or a Standalone application
Widget Caching is always disabled in GlobalInvalidation mode

summary: How to use the UMG RichTextBlock with Data Table style sets (Rich Text Style Row, Rich Image Row), inline markup tags for styles and images, image decorators via RichTextBlockImageRowDecorator, writing custom URichTextBlockDecorator/FRichTextDecorator classes, plus a full property reference.
gotchas: Name the first style row "Default" to make it the default text style
A font must be set on each Rich Text Style Row (enable Show Engine Content to pick Roboto) or text won't display correctly
The RichTextBlock box does not auto-size to text unless Size To Content is enabled
Font size points convert to Slate Units at 96 dpi

summary: Blueprint walkthrough for a draggable HUD element: a DragDropOperation subclass carrying a widget reference and offset, OnMouseButtonDown with Detect Drag If Pressed, OnDragDetected creating the drag visual, and the HUD's OnDrop override repositioning the widget.
gotchas: The HUD Canvas Panel must have Visibility set to Visible to receive the drop hit test
Uncheck Remove DPIScale on Set Position in Viewport in this setup
Extra checks are needed to keep widgets inside safe zones or off other widgets

summary: How-to for setting up the DPI Scale Rule and DPI Curve keys in User Interface Settings so a widget authored at scale 1.0 for one device resolution scales automatically to other device aspect ratios.
gotchas: Author UI at DPI scale 1.0 and let the curve scale it
A second curve key is needed to set a resolution range or the base value is slightly off
Widgets shifting off-screen usually need anchors

summary: Short reference for UMG's resolution-independent DPI scaling settings in Project Settings > User Interface: Application Scale, the four DPI Scale Rule options, and editing or supplying the DPI Curve.

Compares three ways to feed HUD health/energy: function binding (cast every frame), property binding (cache reference in Event Construct, poll value), and event-driven updates via an Event Dispatcher in the character bound to Custom Events in the widget.
gotchas: Function bindings run every frame even when values don't change, which hurts performance in complex UIs

summary: Explains binding widget properties (e.g. Progress Bar Percent, button IsEnabled) to a Blueprint function or a variable via the Bind button so the widget reflects changes automatically.
gotchas: Calling the Set function directly on a bound property breaks the binding

summary: How to create UMG widget animations in the Animations and Timeline panels (+Animation, Auto Key, Add Key, multi-key editing), play/stop them from the graph via the animation variable, with an animated main menu example using Set Timer.
Describes the UMG Clipping property modes (Inherit, Clip to Bounds, Without Intersecting, Always, On Demand) built on Slate clipping and when to use them.
gotchas: Elements in different clipping spaces cannot be batched, so only enable clipping where needed
Without Intersecting cannot escape a parent set to Clip to Bounds - Always
